---
title: "Flagged only by the input"
format:
  html:
    page-layout: full
execute:
  echo: false
---

Observations the input flags bad and nrtqclib passes, over the same
profiles as [Flag differences in NRT](analyses-flags.qmd): at sea, marked
NRT, and not estimated to carry delayed mode flags, each variable over its
own profiles.

The input carries one flag per variable and nothing about which test set
it, so these cannot be traced to a test the way nrtqclib's can. What can
be asked is where they sit in their profiles, which value the input gave
them, and which tests the producers say they run that nrtqclib does not
have. A test that judges a whole profile flags all of it; one that judges
a level flags a point; a check on the start of a cast flags a stretch at
the top.

```{ojs}
//| output: false
app = import(new URL("assets/js/app.js", document.baseURI).href)
meta = app.loadAnalyses()
name = (id) => app.datasetName(meta, id)
table = app.analysisTable
byDataset = (a, b) => app.datasetOrder(meta, a.dataset_id) - app.datasetOrder(meta, b.dataset_id)
variableLabel = (n) => meta.variables.find((v) => v.name === n)?.label ?? n
variableOrder = (n) => meta.variables.findIndex((v) => v.name === n)
byDatasetVariable = (a, b) => byDataset(a, b) || variableOrder(a.variable) - variableOrder(b.variable)
rule = meta ? meta.rules.estimated_delayed : null
shapes = meta ? app.loadAnalysisTable("items_shape") : null
```

```{ojs}
meta === null ? app.analysesMissing() : html``
```

## Tests nrtqclib does not have

From the regional centres' answers, set out on
[Flag differences in NRT](analyses-flags.qmd#what-each-side-runs):

- **Frozen profile**, listed by all three regional centres: a profile almost
  identical to the same platform's previous one, as from a stuck sensor or
  a transmission that repeats itself. It is not the repeated cast removed
  as a [duplicate](analyses-conversion.qmd#duplicates-within-a-product),
  which shares the previous profile's day and position. No sign of it
  shows in the input flags. Where one platform has identical profiles
  hours apart, the regional centres flag every copy or none, never only the
  repeat; and the exact repeats of a platform's previous profile left after
  the duplicate step are hardly ever flagged. The test cannot explain the
  whole profiles below.
- **The Baltic's checks on the whole profile**, run before the tests on
  each variable: negative pressure (a measurement in air), pressure
  increasing from the surface to the bottom, spikes in pressure, and a
  soaking depth left in. Negative pressure and a soaking depth act on the
  start of a cast, so their failures sit at the top of a profile.

The global products are not covered by these answers; their flags come
from the global product's own QC.

## Where they sit in their profiles

Each observation only the input flags is placed against the observations
the input calls good in the same profile, by pressure: above the
shallowest of them, below the deepest, or between them. Between them, it is
either the only one of its profile there or one of several.

```{ojs}
meta ? app.analysisFigure(
  "items_shape_original",
  "Observations only the input flags, by where they sit in their profile against the observations the input calls good: all of the profile, a stretch above the shallowest good level, a stretch below the deepest, or between them, alone or with others. The number at the end of a bar is the observations it is made of.",
  "Stacked bars per product and variable of the share of input-only observations by their place in the profile."
) : html``
```

```{ojs}
meta ? md`**A whole profile here is mostly a short one.** A profile marked NRT whose input flags at least ${Math.round(100 * rule.min_share)}% of its observations, where nrtqclib does not, is estimated to be delayed mode once it has ${rule.min_observations} observations with a usable flag, and leaves this comparison. What stays are profiles too short to be estimated, and profiles nrtqclib flags in part too.` : html``
```

```{ojs}
//| output: false
shapeKeys = meta ? meta.shapes.map((s) => s.key) : []
shapeRows = shapes
  ? [...shapes.filter((r) => r.status === "original_only").reduce((m, r) => {
      const key = `${r.dataset_id}|${r.variable}`;
      const row = m.get(key) ?? {
        key, dataset_id: r.dataset_id, variable: r.variable, n_obs: 0, negative: 0,
        ...Object.fromEntries(shapeKeys.map((k) => [k, 0]))
      };
      row.n_obs += r.n_obs;
      row[r.shape] += r.n_obs;
      if (r.negative_pressure) row.negative += r.n_obs;
      m.set(key, row);
      return m;
    }, new Map()).values()].sort(byDatasetVariable)
  : []
usedShapes = shapeKeys.filter((k) => shapeRows.some((r) => r[k] > 0))
```

```{ojs}
meta ? table(shapeRows, [
  { key: "dataset_id", label: "Product", align: "left", format: name },
  { key: "variable", label: "Variable", align: "left", format: variableLabel },
  { key: "n_obs", label: "Observations" },
  ...usedShapes.map((k) => ({
    key: k,
    label: meta.shapes.find((s) => s.key === k).label,
    format: (_, r) => app.formatSmallShare(r[k], r.n_obs)
  })),
  { key: "negative", label: "At negative pressure", title: "Share recorded at a pressure below 0, above the sea surface", format: (_, r) => app.formatSmallShare(r.negative, r.n_obs) }
]) : html``
```

## Which value the input gave them

A value the input calls probably bad (3) is a softer disagreement than one
it calls bad (4). The 3s are looked at on their own on
[Probably good and probably bad](analyses-probable-flags.qmd).

```{ojs}
flagsTable = meta ? app.loadAnalysisTable("items_original_flags") : null
originalOnly = flagsTable
  ? app.widen(
      flagsTable.filter((r) => r.nrtqclib_bad === false &&
        (meta.variables.find((v) => v.name === r.variable)?.bad_flag_values ?? []).includes(r.original_flag)),
      { index: ["dataset_id", "variable"], column: "original_flag", value: "n_obs", name: (v) => `f${v}` }
    ).sort(byDatasetVariable)
  : []
flagKeys = [...new Set(originalOnly.flatMap((r) => Object.keys(r).filter((k) => /^f\d+$/.test(k))))].sort()
originalRows = originalOnly.map((r) => ({ ...r, n_obs: flagKeys.reduce((sum, k) => sum + (r[k] ?? 0), 0) }))
meta ? table(originalRows, [
  { key: "dataset_id", label: "Product", align: "left", format: name },
  { key: "variable", label: "Variable", align: "left", format: variableLabel },
  { key: "n_obs", label: "Observations" },
  ...flagKeys.map((k) => ({
    key: k,
    label: app.flagWithMeaning(Number(k.slice(1))),
    format: (v, r) => app.formatSmallShare(v ?? 0, r.n_obs)
  }))
]) : html``
```

## By platform

The platforms of one product by the share of their observations only the
input flags, highest first. A disagreement concentrated on a few platforms
points to how those platforms are processed rather than to a test; the
[Platforms](platforms.qmd) page opens their profiles.

```{ojs}
platforms = meta ? app.loadAnalysisTable("items_platforms") : null
viewof platformDataset = meta && platforms
  ? Inputs.select([...new Set(platforms.map((r) => r.dataset_id))], { label: "Product", format: name })
  : html``
```

```{ojs}
// One row per platform; shares kept as percentages so they sort by value.
share = (part, whole) => (whole > 0 ? (100 * part) / whole : null)
platformRows = platforms
  ? [...platforms
      .filter((r) => r.dataset_id === platformDataset)
      .reduce((m, r) => {
        const row = m.get(r.platform_code) ?? { key: r.platform_code, platform_code: r.platform_code };
        row[`${r.variable}_profiles`] = r.n_profiles;
        row[`${r.variable}_n`] = r.n_original_only;
        row[`${r.variable}_share`] = share(r.n_original_only, r.n_obs);
        m.set(r.platform_code, row);
        return m;
      }, new Map()).values()]
  : []
meta && platforms ? table(
  platformRows,
  [
    { key: "platform_code", label: "Platform", align: "left", format: (v) => v },
    ...meta.variables.flatMap((v) => [
      { key: `${v.name}_profiles`, label: `${v.label}: profiles`, format: (x) => (x == null ? "" : app.formatCount(x)) },
      { key: `${v.name}_n`, label: "Original only", format: (x) => (x == null ? "" : app.formatCount(x)) },
      { key: `${v.name}_share`, label: "Share", format: app.formatPercent }
    ])
  ],
  { sortKey: `${meta.variables[0].name}_n`, descending: true }
) : html``
```

## Read together

- **Arctic NRT regional**: nearly all the temperature ones come from one
  platform, TOP-4, so the temperature shares describe that platform: most
  several levels inside the profile, a fifth a stretch at the bottom. The
  salinity ones are spread over more platforms, and half of them are a
  stretch at the bottom. All are flagged 4.
- **Baltic NRT regional**: spread over many platforms, with about a third
  a stretch at the top of the profile and none at negative pressure. That
  fits the soaking depth check the Baltic centre runs on the whole profile
  before its other tests, which nrtqclib does not have.
- **Mediterranean NRT regional**: few observations, all from one platform,
  29SO; most of the temperature ones are a stretch at the top. The
  centre's answers name no test acting on the start of a cast, so the test
  behind them is not known.
- **The global products**: mostly several levels inside the profile, with
  stretches at both ends and some whole short profiles, and a few
  platforms account for a large part of them. Their QC is not described by
  the regional centres, so this page can only describe them. The
  Mediterranean global product is the only one with input-only flags at
  negative pressure.
